text: Adding a million 1.0s to 10^16 leaves it unchanged, but summing them first and then adding gives the right answer. Why?
choices: The gap between adjacent doubles at 10^16 is 2.0, so adding 1 rounds straight back
The loop was optimized away in one case
Floating-point addition is not defined for large values
explanation: A value less than half a step away rounds back to where it started, so each of the million additions was individually discarded. Summing the small values first produces 10^6, which is large enough to survive the addition. This is why floating-point addition is not associative, and why you add small values first.
